canonical_statement: The review compared cardiovascular and kidney effectiveness among five SGLT2 inhibitors across clinically relevant underlying-condition subgroups using a network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
The network meta-analysis included 21 placebo-controlled randomized trials with 96,196 participants.
Across the included trials, 51,964 participants received an SGLT2 inhibitor and 44,232 received placebo.
The evidence base comprised 8 dapagliflozin trials, 6 empagliflozin trials, 3 canagliflozin trials, 3 sotagliflozin trials, and 1 ertugliflozin trial.
Trial follow-up ranged from 3 months to 4.2 years.
Eligible studies were peer-reviewed randomized trials or randomized trial subgroup analyses comparing an SGLT2 inhibitor with placebo.

canonical_statement: The active interventions were empagliflozin, ertugliflozin, dapagliflozin, canagliflozin, and sotagliflozin; doses of the same agent were pooled for the network analysis.
All included randomized comparisons used placebo; the five active agents were connected only indirectly through the common placebo comparator.
The review followed PRISMA guidance for network meta-analysis and was registered in PROSPERO as CRD42023403810.
MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL were searched from inception through August 31, 2023, with a medical librarian involved in the search strategy.
Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and Risk of Bias 2 assessment, resolving disagreements by consensus.
When hazard ratios were available they were extracted; otherwise risk ratios and standard errors were estimated from reported event counts.
Random-effects frequentist network meta-analysis was performed with the netmeta package in R version 4.2.1.
Heterogeneity was assessed with Cochran Q, tau, and I-squared statistics.
Publication bias was examined with funnel plots and Egger tests.
Prespecified subgroup analyses evaluated diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and heart-failure phenotype; chronic kidney disease was defined by eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m2.
Sensitivity analyses excluded EMPA-REG OUTCOME because of its comparatively large treatment effect and excluded VERTIS-CV because it was the only ertugliflozin trial.

The supplementary PRISMA flow reports 4,518 records identified, 2,124 records screened after duplicate removal, 86 full-text reports assessed, 34 full-text reports excluded, 21 randomized trials included, and 52 reports included in the review.
The primary efficacy outcome was the composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure.

concept.text: cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure

canonical_statement: Secondary mortality outcomes included all-cause death and cardiovascular death.
Hospitalization for heart failure was evaluated as a secondary efficacy outcome.
Kidney disease progression was harmonized as a sustained eGFR decrease of at least 50% from randomization, with trial-specific definitions detailed in Supplementary Table S5.

outcome.definition: Sustained eGFR decrease of at least 50% from randomization, harmonized across trial-specific definitions.

canonical_statement: Acute kidney injury was identified using the MedDRA Preferred Term when possible.
Safety outcomes included limb amputation, fracture, hypoglycemia, diabetic ketoacidosis, orthostatic hypotension, urinary tract infection, and genital infection.
Risk of bias was judged low for almost all included randomized trials.
Funnel-plot and Egger-test analyses did not suggest publication bias for the evaluated efficacy and safety networks.
No statistically significant between-agent difference was detected for primary composite of cardiovascular death or heart-failure hospitalization in the overall network.

No statistically significant between-agent difference was detected for cardiovascular death in the overall network.
No statistically significant between-agent difference was detected for hospitalization for heart failure in the overall network.
No statistically significant between-agent difference was detected for kidney disease progression in the overall network.
Empagliflozin was associated with lower acute kidney injury risk than sotagliflozin in the overall network, HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.53 to 0.92).
Dapagliflozin was associated with lower acute kidney injury risk than sotagliflozin in the overall network, HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.56 to 0.96).
For the overall primary composite network, heterogeneity was Q=8.12, p=0.52, tau=0, and I-squared=0%.

Among participants with diabetes, no statistically significant between-agent difference was detected for the primary composite, all-cause death, cardiovascular death, heart-failure hospitalization, or kidney disease progression.
Among participants with diabetes, empagliflozin had lower acute kidney injury risk than sotagliflozin, HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.55 to 1.00).
Among participants with diabetes, dapagliflozin had lower acute kidney injury risk than sotagliflozin, HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.57 to 1.00).
Among participants without diabetes, the available empagliflozin and dapagliflozin data did not show a statistically significant between-agent difference for the evaluated outcomes.
Among participants with chronic kidney disease, no statistically significant between-agent efficacy difference was detected for the evaluated outcomes.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that differences in cardiovascular and kidney effectiveness among the evaluated SGLT2 inhibitors were not consistently statistically significant across underlying conditions.
The authors suggested that empagliflozin might be preferred for patients without chronic kidney disease because several no-CKD contrasts favored empagliflozin.
The authors called for further comparative investigation because the available network evidence did not provide consistent direct evidence of superiority among agents.
In participants without diabetes, only empagliflozin and dapagliflozin were represented, and dapagliflozin often had lower point estimates without statistically significant differences.
In HFrEF, dapagliflozin had the lowest point estimates for several outcomes without statistically significant between-agent differences; this pattern was not reproduced in HFpEF.
Sotagliflozin had the lowest point estimate for genital infection, but between-agent differences were not statistically significant.
The analysis used trial-level aggregate data rather than individual participant data, limiting adjustment for concurrent comorbidities and patient characteristics.
All included randomized comparisons were against placebo, so active-agent comparisons were indirect rather than head-to-head.
Because the network was connected only through placebo and contained no closed loops, between-design inconsistency could not be assessed.
Different doses of the same SGLT2 inhibitor were pooled, which can mask dose-specific differences.
Rare safety outcomes produced wide confidence intervals and unstable comparative estimates.
The large number of network and subgroup comparisons increases the chance of type I error.
The no-diabetes subgroup did not include all five agents and approved dosing differs by indication.
Heart-failure phenotype reporting was incomplete, especially for sotagliflozin and canagliflozin.
